assembly_instructions: 1. Clamp the port and starboard 2.33 m square-tube side rails on a flat jig at the 1.49 m overall track envelope. 2. Bolt or weld the front, middle, and rear cross members between the rails, then check diagonals so the ladder frame is square before adding braces. 3. Install the thin open battery-tray floor, four raised tray rim members, and four diagonal floor braces, leaving the tray top open for module service. 4. Add the front and rear bumper tubes plus four suspension towers and their top tabs, then verify all wheel centers sit at y = 0.30 m so the tires touch the ground plane. 5. Lower six removable battery modules into the tray, fasten the two hold-down straps and terminal blocks, then connect the front and rear copper bus bars to the BMS, DC/DC converter, charge socket, and inverter. 6. Mount the BMS, inverter, DC/DC converter, low-voltage lead, charge-port cable, and inverter-to-motor cable above the open tray where they remain visible without removing a body shell. 7. Assemble each corner with lower A-arm links, upper control-arm links, hub upright, brake disc, brake caliper, wheel rim, tire, damper body, and visible coil spring. 8. Fit the steering rack to the front cross member, connect the tie rods and spherical tie-rod ends to the front uprights, then install the pinion joint, tilted steering column, steering wheel, pedal box, throttle pedal, and brake pedal. 9. Bolt the rear transverse traction motor and single-speed gearbox to the rear cross member, install the output housing, inner CV joints, and both rear half-shafts to the driven hubs. 10. Install the driver and passenger seat rails, thin cushions, back panels, bolsters, and head pads, then perform final checks for wheel-ground contact, tray service clearance, brake-caliper clearance, steering linkage alignment, and a continuous connection path from every part back to the welded frame.

info.japanese_name: TABBY EVO（オープンソース EV プラットフォーム）
info.english_name: Open Motors TABBY EVO — Open-Source Electric Vehicle Platform
info.summary: Italian-designed open-hardware 'skateboard' EV chassis. A modular, rolling platform intended as a starting point for EV startups, OEM concept builds, and university teaching.
info.description: TABBY EVO is the second-generation open-source electric-vehicle platform from OSVehicle / Open Motors. It is a 'skateboard' rolling chassis — a welded/bolted steel space frame with suspension, steering, brakes, battery, motor, and electronics all pre-integrated, ready to take any body shell bolted on top. The architecture follows a rear-drive layout with a single transverse electric motor coupled to a reduction gearbox and a transverse drive shaft to the rear wheels, while the battery pack sits flat under the floor between the front and rear axles. A motor controller, battery management system (BMS), and a DC/DC converter ride on the floor beside the battery; a charge port pierces the side rail. Full CAD, bill of materials, wiring diagrams, and assembly manuals are released under CC BY-SA 4.0 so that others can build, fork, or commercialize the platform.
info.operator: Open Motors community + EV startups using TABBY as a reference chassis
info.contract_value: Reference BOM published; no fixed list price
info.status: Open-source; documents and CAD archived and publicly downloadable

parts.name: Port Longitudinal Side Rail
parts.role: Full-length square-tube rail that forms the port edge of the TABBY EVO ladder frame.

parts.name: Starboard Longitudinal Side Rail
parts.role: Full-length square-tube rail that forms the starboard edge of the TABBY EVO ladder frame.

parts.name: Front Cross Member
parts.role: Forward transverse tube tying both side rails together and carrying the steering rack and front bumper.

parts.name: Middle Battery Cross Member
parts.role: Central transverse tube that keeps the battery tray square under seat and electronics loads.

parts.name: Rear Cross Member
parts.role: Rear transverse tube that supports the motor, gearbox, suspension pick-ups, and rear bumper.

parts.name: Open Battery Tray Floor
parts.role: Thin flat tray floor under the seats; the top is open so individual battery modules remain visible.

parts.name: Battery Tray Front Rim
parts.role: Raised front lip of the serviceable battery tray, preventing module movement under braking.

parts.name: Battery Tray Rear Rim
parts.role: Raised rear lip of the serviceable battery tray, preventing module movement under acceleration.

parts.name: Battery Tray Port Rim
parts.role: Port-side tray lip bolted inside the side rail and pierced by the charge-port cable route.

parts.name: Battery Tray Starboard Rim
parts.role: Starboard tray lip bolted inside the side rail and exposing the battery service opening from above.

parts.name: Front-Port Diagonal Floor Brace
parts.role: Diagonal tube that triangulates the front half of the tray against torsion.

parts.name: Front-Starboard Diagonal Floor Brace
parts.role: Diagonal tube that mirrors the front-port brace and resists steering rack loads.

parts.name: Rear-Port Diagonal Floor Brace
parts.role: Diagonal tube that carries rear powertrain torque into the port side rail.

parts.name: Rear-Starboard Diagonal Floor Brace
parts.role: Diagonal tube that mirrors the rear-port brace and triangulates the motor bay.

parts.name: Front Bumper Tube
parts.role: Round front bumper tube spanning the front of the chassis ahead of the steering rack.

parts.name: Rear Bumper Tube
parts.role: Round rear bumper tube protecting the rear-mounted motor and gearbox.

parts.name: Battery Module Front-Center

parts.name: Battery Module Front-Starboard
parts.role: Removable Li-ion module in the front-right tray bay, accessible without removing a body shell.

parts.name: Battery Module Rear-Port

parts.name: Battery Module Rear-Center
parts.role: Removable Li-ion module in the rear-center tray bay, strapped to the steel tray floor.

parts.name: Battery Module Rear-Starboard

parts.name: Rear Battery Hold-Down Strap

parts.name: Battery Management System
